heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro — advanced foundation models for professional image, video, and multimodal content creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a full-bleed orange-led hero with a soft spotlight and gradient overlay, then place a floating dashboard-style product panel on the right-lower quadrant rather than a standard split. The visual should layer image tiles, video frame strips, audio waveform cues, and model chips to signal enterprise workflow control. Keep the type oversized and confident, with the H1 set in a dramatic 64px+ hierarchy. CTA buttons must be solid Techjockey orange with strong contrast. This should feel premium, operational, and proof-led rather than cinematic or decorative.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a full-bleed, high-contrast hero to immediately match the ad message and establish premium enterprise credibility.
Move from hero into a compact logo-proof band to switch from emotional impact to trust without repeating the same visual treatment.
Use a tabbed product section with preview panel for the first feature block, then an alternating split-panel layout for the second block to break pattern repetition.
Make testimonials visually lighter and more compact than the product sections so the page rhythm shifts from product explanation to proof.
End with a centered, conversion-forward lead form card on a white surface to create a clear closing focal point after denser content.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation for Enterprise Teams
blueprint.metaDescription: Generate high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance models Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Built for professionals and enterprises creating premium visual content.

sections.backgroundTreatment: solid-brand-block with layered dashboard-panels, floating model chips, and subtle depth overlays
sections.designNote: Content-first but dynamic: headline answers what this is, subheadline answers who it is for, and the CTA is explicit and primary. Use an orange-led split hero with a right-side enterprise AI visualization showing image cards, video frame strips, audio wave accents, and model labels for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Keep the copy stacked vertically with a compact benefit list beneath the supporting line. Primary CTA must read exactly 'Get started' in accent orange at 100% opacity.

Place trust immediately after the hero using 3-6 recognisable customer logos if available; if the logo set is weak or unavailable, replace with a clean metric strip. Keep it compact, horizontally aligned, and visually lighter than the hero. This section should feel like an anchored proof band rather than a decorative showcase.

Use a tabbed interface for the two product blocks because both are substantial and feature-rich. First present Seedream 4.5 as the lead tab with a preview panel showing image generation, editing, and composition examples. Then switch to Seedance 1.5 Pro in an alternating split-panel layout to break the rhythm and emphasize audio-video generation. Focus on the 1-2 features most likely to drive the click: for Seedream, high-resolution output and typographic rendering; for Seedance, synchronized audio-visual generation and cinematic camera control. Avoid a flat grid because both sections have 5+ features.

Treat proof as a credibility module, not a social section. Use the strongest 3 testimonials in a compact card grid or spotlight trio, emphasizing enterprise creative control, faster turnaround, and synchronized audio-video storytelling. Keep the cards plain with light framing and minimal embellishment so the focus stays on outcomes.

Reserve this section for deeper feature explanation after proof, but keep it visually distinct from the earlier product block. Use an accordion with a persistent visual preview panel so users can scan capabilities without cognitive overload. Alternate the emphasis between image and video capabilities so adjacent blocks never feel identical. Maintain a strong enterprise tone and avoid generic SaaS feature language.

Present pricing as a decision-support block rather than a generic plan table. Use two centered cards with the image model first and the video model second, highlighting the quoted starting price only where supplied. Keep CTA labeling consistent across the page with 'Get started' on all buttons, and preserve orange solid-button styling.

Close with a dense but visually clean lead-capture card that feels like the final conversion step. The form should sit in a bordered, floating panel with strong hierarchy, minimal distractions, and a single full-width mobile CTA labeled exactly 'Get started'. Keep it lighter than the product sections but stronger than the proof section so the ending feels decisive.
Do not use a marquee. If needed, place a static horizontal logo strip or omit entirely. This should not compete with the main proof band or CTA. Keep it subtle and secondary.

blueprint.designPersonality: Confident, intelligent, and commercially credible. The page should feel like a premium AI workflow platform for enterprise buyers: highly structured, visually rich, and proof-led, with logos as the primary trust signal and orange as the unmistakable brand anchor.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use an enterprise-style AI product visualization: layered output previews, model capability cards, generation timelines, waveform and frame-strip accents, and floating chips for image, video, audio, and multimodal workflows. Avoid futuristic neon or purple gradients; instead keep the visual language crisp, white, orange-led, and dashboard-like.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and product-specific, so 48px keeps it readable and premium without breaking the layout.

colours.colourReason: Brand colours are locked to Techjockey’s palette, so the page uses the exact orange primary for hero and CTAs, white for clarity, and deep neutral text for enterprise readability.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-column, high-impact hero with logo anchor, large headline, compact supporting copy, and a short benefit list; content is stacked vertically with strong top-to-bottom hierarchy rather than split-screen media.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Banner/hero first, then a lead-capture form block, followed by detailed product sections; overall flow is linear and conversion-driven with one primary action per section.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Mostly plain content blocks with light framing rather than decorative cards; form content sits in a bordered/contained panel, while feature lists are presented as simple stacked rows or bullets.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: One dominant primary CTA in the hero and contextual secondary CTAs on feature sections; CTAs are placed after concise value statements and repeated at decision points.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No visible pricing module in the reference structure.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer not represented in the provided markup.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage in the visible structure; logo is used as a small trust/brand mark, with optional carousel/banner media implied by commented code but not active in the shown state.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Feature-led sections with a label, headline, descriptive paragraph, and a list of capability bullets; supports progressive disclosure by expanding from overview to specific benefits.
referenceMap.formPattern: Prominent lead form card directly under the hero, optimized for conversion with a clear heading and multiple hidden tracking fields; the form is dense in metadata but visually straightforward.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static presentation-first layout; no active motion patterns are evident in the visible markup, though the structure suggests carousel support was considered but disabled.
designNotes: Prioritize a strong first-screen hierarchy with concise benefits and a single conversion path.
Use stacked sections and restrained visuals for enterprise credibility.
Keep feature sections scannable with labels, headlines, and bullets.
If media is added, keep it secondary to copy and CTA.
Maintain generous whitespace and clear separation between hero, form, and feature detail blocks.

designStrategy.reasoning: This page is best positioned as a high-intent demo-booking experience for professional buyers evaluating two closely related generative AI products. The audience is solution-aware, so the design should lead with product value, then quickly reinforce trust through logos-first proof, followed by structured feature storytelling. Because the content is long and enterprise-oriented, a balanced, centered hero with strong messaging will keep the page focused and easy to scan. The conversion path should be medium-aggressive: clear primary CTA repetition without feeling pushy. Since the reference behavior and memory stress complete page delivery, sticky top trust/navigation treatment and a full-page, scrollable structure are essential.
